en: The Philippines officially has 7,641 islands, but only about 2,000 of these islands are actually inhabited by people.
Taal Volcano features a unique structure where its main crater is actually a lake containing a smaller island.
Mount Hamiguitan hosts a unique pygmy forest where century-old trees only grow a few meters tall due to harsh conditions.
The Philippine tarsier has giant eyes that are actually as large as its entire brain to help it see at night.
The Banaue Rice Terraces were carved into the steep mountains of Ifugao entirely by hand over 2,000 years ago.
The Sierra Madre mountain range stretches over 1,000 kilometers along eastern Luzon to act as a natural shield against typhoons.
Lake Lanao is one of only two ancient lakes in the Philippines, meaning it has existed since before the ice ages.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River is a massive underground river that flows completely inside a cave before reaching the sea.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park is a remote marine sanctuary in the Sulu Sea protecting over 600 species of fish.
The Philippine eagle is one of the largest and most powerful eagles in the world, featuring a massive wingspan of up to two meters.
The Callao Cave in Cagayan contains a massive natural chapel illuminated by a skylight, where some of the oldest human remains in the Philippines were discovered.
Mount Mayon in Albay is famous for having a nearly perfect symmetrical cone shape, making it a highly photographed volcano.
